meta.case_name: Pay Me My Money, In Cash

prompt.context: COVID has fundamentally changed the MBA experience for students. Classes are mostly remote, travel has been eliminated, and the students are not happy. However, Columbia Business School (CBS) is still charging the same tuition as before COVID. Our client is a group of CBS students who feel that they are not getting the full value of their MBA. In the view of our clients, the MBA is as much about the relationships built with classmates and the experiences gained as it is about the education. Some of our clients were even placed on probation by the school for traveling. They are extremely unhappy.
prompt.question: How do we approach pressuring the school into giving our clients a tuition reduction?

clarifying_info.q: What do we want to accomplish?
clarifying_info.a: Our clients want at least 20% of tuition refunded or reduced, removal of the character probation they received, and an apology from the school for putting them on probation. These demands are absolute and non-negotiable.

clarifying_info.q: Who is the decision-maker on reducing tuition?
clarifying_info.a: Decisions on tuition reduction, removal of probation, and issuing an official apology are all made by the Office of the President of Columbia University.

clarifying_info.q: Is there any particular time this needs to be accomplished by?
clarifying_info.a: Since most of the students are in their 2nd year, they would like their refund before tuition is due at the end of January in the Spring Semester.

clarifying_info.q: What do the students intend to do with the refund?
clarifying_info.a: We don't have any information around that.

clarifying_info.q: Does the school have a history of giving tuition refunds?
How does this year's tuition compare with last year's?
clarifying_info.a: The school announced a tuition freeze last Spring Semester. It is the same as the year before.

clarifying_info.q: Can you tell me more about the coalition of students?
clarifying_info.a: Due to confidentiality, we can provide no details beyond that the client is a coalition of like-minded students.

clarifying_info.q: Has the school responded to their initial demands?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, Columbia University announced there will be no refunds.

framework: 1. Client Demands to School: (a) 20% Tuition Refund ($15k) — explore reduction in tuition (% of students paying full tuition) and increased financial aid; (b) Removal of Probation — influence Provost; (c) Apology From School — consider content and who is apologizing
2. CBS Compared to Peer School Actions: (a) Ivy League/M7 B-Schools — travel restrictions, punishments, violations reported, COVID rate; (b) Near-Peer Schools

3. Potential Client Actions: (a) Tuition Strike — refuse to pay; (b) Donation Withholding — 5-year promise, permanent pledge; (c) Legal Actions — threaten to sue, take to court; (d) Direct Communication with School — email blasts, phone calls; (e) Petition — % of class, alumni; (f) Media Pressure — journalism fellows, TV contacts
4. Risks: (a) CU withholds degree; (b) More negative attention on clients

questions.prompt: Legal Recourse: What ways can we use threats of lawsuits to pressure Columbia University into giving in?
questions.guidance: Litigation against a billion-dollar institution would take too long and would be prohibitively expensive. There is no legal standing for an effective lawsuit and the school is unmoved by threats. This avenue is a dead end.

questions.prompt: Direct Communication with Columbia University: How can we pressure the administration to apologize, overturn the punishment, and reduce tuition?
questions.guidance: The Provost of Columbia University issued the punishment and is unmoved by any appeals. Direct communication has no leverage here.

questions.prompt: Donation Withholding: How can we leverage not donating to pressure the school?
questions.guidance: The University already considers the current students a lost cause for donations, so this lever has no effect.

questions.prompt: Tuition Strike: How can we leverage going on tuition strike to pressure the school?
questions.guidance: The University has stated that if students refuse to pay their tuition, they will neither confer their degrees nor allow the students to earn credits for the semester. This backfires on the clients.

questions.prompt: Petition: How would we go about getting a petition signed, by whom, and how would we use it?
questions.guidance: Our clients already attempted a petition, and the school is unmoved.

questions.prompt: Media Pressure: How could we use the media to pressure the school into giving in to our client's demands?
questions.guidance: Bringing media attention to clients who traveled overseas and partied during a global pandemic is in poor taste and will likely result in more negative attention on clients. For those who did not travel, being students at an Ivy League institution draws no public sympathy. This approach is counterproductive.

questions.prompt: Peer Schools: How can we use the actions of peer schools to pressure Columbia?
questions.guidance: No peer or near-peer school has given a tuition reduction. They also have similar travel punishment policies and will not help our clients.

questions.prompt: Student Walkout: How could we plan and execute a walkout to pressure the school?
questions.guidance: If students don't attend class, they will receive Incompletes as grades and be unable to graduate. This is also unpopular with the broader student body and disrespectful to professors who are uninvolved in the punishment.

questions.prompt: Targeting Alumni Support: How can we connect with CBS Alumni and motivate them to pressure the school?
questions.guidance: The alumni overwhelmingly support the school in this matter and are not sympathetic to the clients. Many have lost family members and friends to the pandemic and are upset with the clients' behavior.

brainstorming.prompt: What additional pressure tactics could the coalition of students pursue to force the university to meet their demands?

categories.name: Legal Actions
ideas: Engage a high-profile attorney for publicity

categories.name: Financial Leverage
ideas: Organize a tuition strike — refuse to pay
Pledge to withhold future alumni donations (5-year promise or permanent pledge)

categories.name: Direct Communication
ideas: Organized phone campaigns to university offices
Request meetings with the Office of the President

categories.name: Collective Action
ideas: Circulate a petition among current students

categories.name: Media & Public Pressure
ideas: Engage journalism fellows in the student body
Leverage TV contacts for news coverage

categories.name: Benchmarking Peer Schools
ideas: Research Ivy League/M7 travel restriction policies
Identify if any peer school gave refunds or lifted punishments
Use favorable peer comparisons as negotiating leverage

recommendation: Advise the client to drop their appeals to the school and accept that the demands cannot be met.
risks: The clients will likely be extremely upset that there is nothing that can be done and may push back on this recommendation.
next_steps: Communicate clearly to the clients that all reasonable avenues have been explored without success.
Advise the clients to finish out their degrees, fulfill their tuition obligations, and move on.
